مَرْمُومٌ sing. of مَرَامِيمٌ, (TA,) which is [an epithet] applied to arrows, meaning Having the feathers repaired, or put into a good state. (K, TA.) ―
-b2- And (tropical:) An arrow [made even, or straight, by means of the eye; or] looked at until made even, or straight. (TA.) ―
-b3- You say also, أَمْرُ فُلَانٍ مَرْمُومٌ [i. e. The affair, or case, of such a one is rectified, or repaired]. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
